articleTitle: Non-linear/non-Gaussian filtering and the bootstrap filter
abstract: The bootstrap filter is a random sample (stochastic simulation) based approach to implementing general Bayesian filters. The central idea of this approach is to represent the required p.d.f. by a set of random samples, rather than as a functional form over state space. This technique is able to cope with any functional nonlinearity and system and measurement noise of any distribution. There are also significant reparameterisation and p.d.f. summarisation advantages of a sample based approach. We outline the bootstrap filter approach together with several techniques for improving the efficiency of the basic algorithm and then present a Monte Carlo analysis of a bearings-only tracking problem to illustrate performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Normalised order statistic LMS adaptive filtering
abstract: Normalised order statistic adaptive filtering is proposed to overcome the practical problem of spike clustering. The family of Order Statistic Least Mean Square (OSLMS) adaptive filter algorithms is substantially more robust to single, well-spaced, outlier values present within the signals which form the input to an adaptive filter than the established Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm. Normalisation of the LMS algorithm is another, not so generally appreciated, mechanism which affords such robustness in an adaptive algorithm. Moreover, for outliers which cluster it is computationally more efficient to combine the benefits of an order statistic adaptive algorithm with normalisation. This leads to the notion of Normalised Order Statistic Least Mean Square (NOSLMS) adaptive filtering. In particular, the Normalised Averaged Least Mean Square (NALMS) and Normalised Median Least Mean Square (NMLMS) algorithms are developed and their performance is demonstrated by application to a parameter estimation problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of simple non-linear recursive smoothing filters
abstract: This paper describes and analyses a particular class of recursive non-linear filters, which are well suited to smoothing applications, and are computationally inexpensive. We restrict our attention to l-D filtering. An application is discussed in which the simplest (first order) filter of this class is effective. Then this first order recursive non-linear filter is described and analysed. Finally, higher-order non-linear recursive smoothing filters are investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Smoothing one dimensional signals using sieves and weightless neural nets
abstract: An adaptive nonlinear filter is described. It is demonstrated to generalise over both standard linear and nonlinear filters and to reject noise from smoothly changing and discontinuous signals. It is placed in the context of a nonlinear multiscale decomposition, sieve, that can be used to characterise nonlinear filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New non-linear decision feedback equalizers based on the functional-link neural network
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for the Decision Feedback Equalizer using the Functional Link Network (DFFLE) for channel equalization in digital communication systems. Results show that the new non-linear DFFLE structures offer superior performance to the Multi-Layered perceptron (MLP) based DFE and the conventional DFE-LMS which are two widely used decision feedback equalizers. The performance has been evaluated in terms of the equalizers' speed of convergence and bit error rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A reduced complexity sub-optimal nonlinear predictor
abstract: In this paper radial basis function (RBF) and Volterra series (VS) nonlinear predictors are examined with a view to reducing their complexity while maintaining prediction performance. A geometrical interpretation is presented which results in a predictor which although suboptimal is of considerably reduced complexity. The geometric interpretation indicates that while a multiplicity of choices of reduced state predictors exists, some choices are better than others in terms of the numerical conditioning of the solution. Two algorithms are developed using this signal subspace approach to find reduced state solutions which are "close to" the minimum norm solution and which share its numerical properties. The performance of these algorithms is assessed using chaotic time series as test signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of robust types of mode filter for signal and image processing applications
abstract: This paper considers filters which can be used for mode estimation. It starts by studying a method which has been used for mode filtering of images, and then goes on to a more systematic analysis covering the rapidly advancing field of robust statistics. It demonstrates the importance of clarifying the specification of the required filter. It has listed five parameters that are important in the design of peak location filters, and has also shown some of the tradeoffs that exist between them. The need to adapt a filter in an appropriate way to cope with specific signals has been demonstrated: there remains the possibility of making filters self-adapting in this way. Finally, the paper provides cogent arguments against the LMedS approach being the 'ultimate' method of mode estimation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

Two adaptive non-linear filters that employ both temporal and amplitude processing have been presented. The application of these filters as a digital channel equaliser has been demonstrated. It has been shown that this class of filters can provide superior performance over their linear counterpart. In general the microstatistic filter requires more weight updates compared with N out of N2 for the amplitude banded filter. The selection of threshold level is rather ad-hoc. They are fixed and are equally spaced throughout the filter operation. Future work is focused on examining dynamic thresholding schemes that can adjust to varying signal range, continuously update the number of threshold levels and vary the distance between quantisation levels throughout the filter operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
